rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A wavefront is a surface of equal phase, and rays stand perpendicular to it. Huygens' principle rebuilds the next wavefront as the forward envelope of wavelets from every point. Reflection and refraction are that envelope in a new direction or a new speed.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A wavefront is the surface that joins points of the wave which oscillate in step. A ray is the direction of travel, perpendicular to the wavefront.  ·  A point source in a uniform medium sends out spherical wavefronts. Very far away a small patch of that sphere is nearly a plane, which is why a distant source is drawn as parallel rays.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Huygens' construction says that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets. The new wavefront, a little time later, is the surface tangent to those wavelets, the forward envelope.  ·  The wavelets also have a backward envelope. Huygens' original picture needs an extra inclination factor, taught later, to cancel the backward wave. At this level you draw the forward envelope.  ·  The construction explains reflection and refraction. The wavelets from the points that have already hit a mirror rebuild a reflected plane wave at the law-of-reflection angle. Entering a slower medium, the wavelets are smaller and the wavefront tilts, which is Snell's law.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A wavefront is not a ray.  ·  The envelope is the new wavefront, not one wavelet.  ·  The backward wave is not drawn at this level.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Refraction tilts the wavefront because the speed changes.  ·  Draw the envelope, not a single wavelet, as the answer.  ·  The speed belongs to the medium the wavelet is in.
